1.why: MFA routes use owner()/pendingOwner() which bind the session’s user id to accountIds and never accept an external account identifier.

2.why: OTP, identity, and backup checks use the secret/hashes of the session’s own account, so a code does not validate for a different user.

3.why: mfa/confirm only sets a.mfa and stores the secret; it does not delete or downgrade other existing auth sessions for that account.

4.why: OTP secret is stored via AES-256-GCM enc(); backup codes are stored as PBKDF2 hashes with salt and pepper.

5.why: Secrets, session ids, backup codes, and identity codes come from crypto.randomBytes/randomInt.

6.why: Session id is only in an HttpOnly cookie; no localStorage/sessionStorage or non-HttpOnly cookie writes for secrets/OTPs/tokens.

7.why: Email is normalized/regex-limited; OTP and recovery codes are matched against strict server-side patterns before use.

8.why: Client rendering sets textContent only; API responses are JSON, so markup in inputs is not executed.

9.why: Handler never issues redirects or Location headers, so no open-redirect path exists.

10.why: headers() sets CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options DENY and frame-ancestors 'none'.

11.why: sessionCookie() sets HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict on the session cookie.

12.why: Stack traces are generic and tokens stay out of URLs, but mock OTP/identity/backup codes are returned to the client and console.log’d.

13.why: Identity codes are one-time with CHALLENGE expiry; TOTP steps are recorded in usedTotp/used; backups flip used and carry expires.

14.why: recordFailure locks identity, source, account, and enrollment limits after 5 failures for LOCK duration.

15.why: signin/verify and mfa/verify delete the old session and issue a new id; idle/absolute timeouts apply; logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
